records.issue_text: BlockedEmail stats write (record.save) inside model validation increments match_count on every validation pass, making tracking data unreliable
records.rationale: `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` during validation (`validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` in `user.rb`). `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs a write side effect: it increments `record.match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and `record.save`. Because validations can run multiple times for the same record/email (e.g., repeated `valid?` calls, failed saves with re-validation), the stats will be incremented on each validation pass rather than on a single “blocked email encountered” event, making `match_count`/`last_match_at` potentially inaccur
records.stripped_text: BlockedEmail stats write (record.save) inside model validation increments match_count on every validation pass, making tracking data unreliable

records.issue_text: Client uses generic user.email.invalid message instead of the existing user.email.blocked translation, giving users in a blocked-email loop a misleading 'invalid' message
records.rationale: The client-side validation for previously rejected emails hardcodes the generic message `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` instead of using the new blocked-email message. In `create_account_controller.js`, when `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` it returns `{ failed: true, reason: I18n.t('user.email.invalid') }`, and `rejectedEmails` is populated whenever the server returns `result.errors.email` (`pushObject(result.values.email)`). Meanwhile the server introduces a specific translation `user.email.blocked` and the validator adds that error (`record.errors.add(attribute, I18n.t(:'user.email.blocked')
records.stripped_text: Client uses generic user.email.invalid message instead of the existing user.email.blocked translation, giving users in a blocked-email loop a misleading 'invalid' message

records.issue_text: Case-sensitive blocked-email lookup and unique index allows bypass by re-registering with different email casing; emails should be normalized to lowercase on write and lookup
records.rationale: BlockedEmail matching is an exact, case-sensitive lookup (`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` in `BlockedEmail.should_block?`), and there is no normalization (e.g., `downcase`) in either `BlockedEmail` or the new `EmailValidator` before calling `should_block?(value)`. The migration adds a unique index on `blocked_emails.email`, which (in typical DB collations) is also case-sensitive, allowing `Foo@bar.com` and `foo@bar.com` as distinct records and allowing a user to bypass blocking by changing email casing.
records.stripped_text: Case-sensitive blocked-email lookup and unique index allows bypass by re-registering with different email casing; emails should be normalized to lowercase on write and lookup

records.issue_text: Regex built from email_domains_blacklist/whitelist settings only escapes dots, so special regex chars can raise RegexpError and take down all user creation; blast radius increased by moving to shared validator
records.rationale: In the new shared `EmailValidator`, `email_in_restriction_setting?` builds a regex from the `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist/blacklist` value by only escaping dots: `domains = setting.gsub('.', '\.')` then `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb). If the setting contains other regex metacharacters (e.g., `[`/`]`, `(`, `|`, `\`), `Regexp.new` can raise `RegexpError`, which would break validation/user creation. This risk existed in the removed `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`, but it remains (and is now in a shared validator).
records.stripped_text: Regex built from email_domains_blacklist/whitelist settings only escapes dots, so special regex chars can raise RegexpError and take down all user creation; blast radius increased by moving to shared validator

records.issue_text: Front-end treats all email errors as 'blocked', showing wrong message and permanently locking out email in rejectedEmails without removal path
records.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, on any failed signup where `result.errors.email` is present, the controller unconditionally adds `result.values.email` to `rejectedEmails` (`pushObject(result.values.email)`). Later, `emailValidation` checks `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` and forces validation failure with the generic message `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')`. This both (a) ignores the specific server-side email error (e.g., `user.email.not_allowed` vs `user.email.blocked` vs uniqueness), and (b) provides no path to remove an email from `rejectedEmails` within the controller lifecycle, effecti
records.stripped_text: Front-end treats all email errors as 'blocked', showing wrong message and permanently locking out email in rejectedEmails without removal path

records.issue_text: Message field text drift in error response contract may affect external consumers parsing human-readable messages
records.rationale: The diff does not change the `message` field contents/format in the error JSON response; it remains `message: I18n.t("login.errors", errors: user.errors.full_messages.join("\n"))` (only adding a trailing comma and new fields `errors:` and `values:`). So the claimed “message field text drift” is contradicted by the unchanged `message:` line in `app/controllers/users_controller.rb`.
records.stripped_text: Message field text drift in error response contract may affect external consumers parsing human-readable messages

records.issue_text: Migration schema requires action_type/match_count non-null with no DB default, so direct SQL/bulk inserts will fail while spec says bulk load is intended method
records.rationale: The migration sets `action_type` as `null: false` with **no DB default** (`t.integer :action_type, null: false`), so a direct SQL/manual/bulk insert that only provides `email` would fail, even though the model sets defaults via `before_validation :set_defaults` (which bulk inserts bypass). The finding’s claim about `match_count` lacking a default is not supported because the migration includes `default: 0` (`t.integer :match_count, null: false, default: 0`).
records.stripped_text: Migration schema requires action_type/match_count non-null with no DB default, so direct SQL/bulk inserts will fail while spec says bulk load is intended method
